claims.statement: Root cause: Carrier partition 2 pickup-window feed consumer failure (stopped 05:58, 47+ min behind). This is an infrastructure failure, not an allocation logic defect.
claims.limitation: None - verified by evidence that reverting allocation logic did not resolve the issue

claims.statement: v18 allocation rule is correct; reverting it did not fix held orders. ANY order routed to partition 2 gets stuck, proving the issue is downstream feed failure, not upstream allocation logic.

Contributing factor: v18 concentrated 186 split-reservation multi-node orders to partition 2, amplifying the impact of partition 2's feed failure. But feed failure is the root cause; v18 merely exposed it.
claims.limitation: v18 may have triggered or exacerbated feed failure but is not the root cause

claims.statement: Impact: 186 orders held; 3,900 collateral allocations reshuffled with duplicates from failed mitigation attempt; partition 2 continues to accept orders that will immediately get stuck.

contradictions.claim_a: c5_02 (v18 allocation rule has defect in slot assignment)
contradictions.claim_b: c8_02 (v18 allocation logic is correct; reverting did not fix held orders)
contradictions.description: Evidence from m8_r_revert demonstrates that the allocation logic is correct; the root cause is partition 2's feed consumer, not v18's algorithm. Initial hypothesis was incorrect.

next_action.rationale: Root cause is definitively established: Carrier partition 2 feed consumer failure (stalled at 05:58, 47+ min behind). This is an infrastructure/operational issue owned by Carrier Operations, not an allocation or application logic issue. Mitigation requires: (1) Carrier Operations to diagnose and restart partition 2 feed consumer, (2) Clear queue and allow feed to catch up, (3) After feed recovery, apply targeted slot correction to partition 2, (4) Replay the 186 stuck orders. The allocation system performed correctly; the failure is upstream in the carrier data pipeline.
